es: Reconocer y usar ecos (Did you?, Have you?) y fichas como Fair enough o No way! para mostrar interés, sorpresa o aceptación, y distinguirlos de las question tags.

teaching.en: “I've just joined a choir that rehearses on Thursday nights.” “Have you? I never knew you could sing, to be honest.”
teaching.es: «Acabo de unirme a un coro que ensaya los jueves por la noche.» «¿Ah, sí? No sabía que cantabas, la verdad.»
teaching.explanationEs: Have you? repite el auxiliar de I've: es un eco que muestra interés y no pide ningún dato.
segments: “I've just joined a choir that rehearses on Thursday nights.” “Have
you? I never knew you could sing, to be honest.”
teaching.audioText: “I've just joined a choir that rehearses on Thursday nights.” “Have you? I never knew you could sing, to be honest.”

teaching.en: “My colleague didn't land a promotion after all.” “Didn't she? I thought her interview had gone really well.”
teaching.es: «Mi colega no consiguió el ascenso, al final.» «¿No? Yo creía que su entrevista había ido muy bien.»
teaching.explanationEs: Didn't she? conserva la polaridad negativa de didn't: es un eco de sorpresa, no una tag.
segments: “My colleague didn't land a promotion after all.” “Didn't
she? I thought her interview had gone really well.”
teaching.audioText: “My colleague didn't land a promotion after all.” “Didn't she? I thought her interview had gone really well.”

teaching.en: “Honestly, I'd turn down an offer that meant moving abroad.” “Fair enough. That depends on what you'd be giving up, I suppose.”
teaching.es: «Sinceramente, yo rechazaría una oferta que implicara mudarme al extranjero.» «Está bien. Supongo que depende de lo que dejarías atrás.»
teaching.explanationEs: Fair enough acepta la postura del otro sin darle la razón ni discutirla.
segments: “Honestly, I'd turn down an offer that meant moving abroad.” “Fair
enough. That depends on what you'd be giving up, I suppose.”
teaching.audioText: “Honestly, I'd turn down an offer that meant moving abroad.” “Fair enough. That depends on what you'd be giving up, I suppose.”

teaching.en: Good banter depends on playful echoes such as “You didn't!” or “No way!”, which tease a friend without ever sounding unkind.
teaching.es: Las buenas bromas entre amigos dependen de ecos juguetones como «¡No me digas!» o «¡No puede ser!», que pican sin resultar desagradables.
teaching.explanationEs: No way! puede expresar incredulidad o admiración: decide el contexto y el tono.
segments: Good banter depends on playful echoes such as “You didn't!” or
“No way!”, which tease a friend without ever sounding unkind.
teaching.audioText: Good banter depends on playful echoes such as “You didn't!” or “No way!”, which tease a friend without ever sounding unkind.

teaching.en: A noncommittal “Mm” gives nothing away, and a listener who only says that can come across as bored, however closely he listens.
teaching.es: Un «Mm» evasivo no revela nada, y quien solo dice eso puede dar la impresión de estar aburrido, por muy atento que esté.
teaching.explanationEs: Sin eco ni pregunta de seguimiento, la escucha atenta puede parecer desinterés.
segments: A noncommittal “Mm” gives nothing away, and a listener who only
says that can come across as bored, however closely he listens.
teaching.audioText: A noncommittal “Mm” gives nothing away, and a listener who only says that can come across as bored, however closely he listens.

teaching.en: “Guess what? My colleague is going to train for a marathon this autumn.” “Is she? Good for her, that takes real dedication.”
teaching.es: «¿A que no sabes qué? Mi colega va a entrenar para una maratón este otoño.» «¿Ah, sí? Me alegro por ella, eso exige mucha dedicación.»
teaching.explanationEs: Guess what? abre un tema con una noticia; el eco Is she? reacciona con interés.
segments: “Guess what? My colleague is going to train for a marathon
this autumn.” “Is she? Good for her, that takes real dedication.”
teaching.audioText: “Guess what? My colleague is going to train for a marathon this autumn.” “Is she? Good for her, that takes real dedication.”

prompt.es: Completa el eco: «¿Ah, sí? Debes de sentirte orgulloso. ¿Qué implicaría?»

feedback.es: La frase original usa have (I've been asked, I've said), así que el eco repite ese auxiliar con you y mantiene la polaridad afirmativa.

hint.es: Busca el auxiliar de la primera frase y repítelo con you.

origin.text: “I've been asked to lead the choir next term, and I've already said yes.” “___ you? You must be proud. What would it involve?”

prompt.es: ¿Qué réplica de Tom es un eco que muestra interés por la noticia de Mia?

choices.text: Does he? That must be really annoying.
Didn't he? That must be really annoying.
Did he? That sounds great, then.
Hasn't he? That must be really annoying.

feedback.es: La frase es negativa y en pasado simple: el eco conserva didn't con el pronombre he. Cambiar el auxiliar o el tiempo rompe el eco.

hint.es: Repite didn't con el pronombre correcto y mantén el mismo tiempo.

origin.text: Mia: “My brother didn't pass his driving test again, and he has already paid for the next one.” Tom: “...”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Está bien, pero yo seguiría rechazando una oferta así.»

answer.text: Fair enough, but I would still turn down an offer like that
accepted: Fair enough, but I would still turn down an offer like that
I would still turn down an offer like that, but fair enough

feedback.es: Fair enough acepta la postura del otro y but introduce tu propia decisión: turn down an offer es la colocación habitual para rechazar.

hint.es: Empieza con la ficha de aceptación y deja la colocación turn down an offer junta.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada intervención con lo que hace quien la dice.

pairs: Have you? Since when do you run?

pairs.es: Muestra interés y pide más datos

pairs: You've lost weight, haven't you?

pairs.es: Pide confirmar lo que ya cree

pairs: Fair enough, I can see your point.
Guess what? I've been offered a new job.

pairs.es: Abre un tema con una noticia

feedback.es: El eco muestra interés, la tag pide confirmar, Fair enough acepta sin discutir y Guess what? anuncia una noticia.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo se siente Tom ante la respuesta de su colega.

choices.text: Offended, because she doubts that he can finish the race.
Relieved, because she does not ask him any more questions.
Let down, because her reply sounds polite but rather cold.
Pleased, because she wishes him luck so warmly.

feedback.es: El eco Have you? va sin pregunta de seguimiento y con la atención puesta en el celular: suena educado pero frío, y por eso Tom se siente decepcionado.

origin.audio: Tom told his colleague that he had decided to train for a marathon. “Have you?” she said, without looking up from her phone. “Mm. Good luck with that.” Tom's smile vanished. He had hoped she would at least ask how long he had been running.

prompt.es: Completa: «Nunca pregunta nada y, aunque escucha, da la impresión de estar aburrido.»

feedback.es: Come across as + adjetivo es la colocación para la impresión que das a los demás; across es la única partícula que la forma.

origin.text: Leo never asks a follow-up question, so even when he is listening carefully he tends to come ___ as rather bored. It is less a matter of manners than of habit.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender el narrador sobre la reacción de Mia.

choices.text: She disagreed with his decision but preferred not to say so.
She was more interested in her food than in Carlos himself.
She had already heard about the offer from Sara earlier.
Her answer was polite but failed to show the curiosity Carlos wanted.

feedback.es: Fair enough acepta sin preguntar nada: por eso la noticia «falls flat». Carlos no se queja de desacuerdo, sino de falta de curiosidad.

origin.audio: At the dinner on Friday, Carlos announced that he had turned down an offer from another firm. “Did you?” said Sara at once, leaning forward. “Why on earth would you do that?” Mia, on the other hand, only said “Mm, fair enough” and went on cutting her bread. Carlos noticed the difference. He had expected the sort of banter they usually shared, the teasing and the sudden “No way!”, and instead he felt that his news had fallen flat. Later, in the kitchen, Mia asked whether he was upset. “Not upset,” he said. “Just surprised that you weren't curious.”

prompt.es: En este fragmento, ¿qué hace exactamente «Have you?» de Leo?

choices.text: Responds with interest to news she has just announced.
Asks her to confirm something he already believes.
Opens a new topic unrelated to her news.
Shows that he doubts the job offer is genuine.

feedback.es: Have you? repite have de I've been offered y reacciona a la noticia; la petición de confirmación ya la había hecho Leo con la tag haven't you?

origin.text: Over coffee, Leo asked his colleague, “You've been to Porto, haven't you?” She nodded and added, “Twice. Guess what? I'm going back in June, because I've been offered a job there.” “Have you? Good for you,” said Leo, though he wondered whether she would accept it.

prompt.es: Completa: «Fue una reunión larga, ¿verdad?»

feedback.es: La tag invierte la polaridad del verbo: was (afirmativo) → wasn't it? Sirve para pedir confirmación, no para mostrar sorpresa.

origin.text: Nobody said a word during the last hour. It was a long meeting, ___ it?

prompt.es: Ordena la réplica a «I've been training for ages»: «¿Ah, sí? ¿Cuánto llevas?»

answer.text: Have you? How long have you been training

feedback.es: Primero el eco con have (el auxiliar de I've been) y después una pregunta de seguimiento con el mismo tiempo verbal.

prompt.es: ¿Qué se deduce de la reacción de Tom ante la noticia de Sara?

choices.text: He was annoyed by her success and wanted to spoil her evening.
His reply was polite, yet it showed little real interest in her news.
He had not understood that she was talking about a promotion.
He was thrilled but too shy to say so in front of everyone.

feedback.es: El tono plano y el cambio inmediato de tema indican cortesía sin interés; el texto no dice que Tom sintiera celos ni que no entendiera.

origin.text: When Sara described the promotion she had just landed, Tom answered “Right. Good for you.” in a flat voice and immediately asked whether anyone had seen the match. Sara laughed it off, but she did not mention her news again all evening, and she left earlier than usual.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige con qué propósito pregunta Ana si Leo irá a escucharlos.

choices.text: To prove that she was right and that he could sing.
To change the subject because the topic bored her.
To keep him involved without pressing him to join.
To make him feel guilty about refusing her invitation.

feedback.es: Ana acepta su decisión con fair enough y le ofrece una forma más suave de participar, sin insistir; Leo la considera una invitación amable, no una presión.

origin.audio: Leo explained that he would rather not join the choir, since he could not sing very well. “Fair enough,” said Ana, “although you never know until you try.” She did not insist. Instead she asked whether he would come and listen on Thursday, which, Leo thought, was a much kinder way of inviting him.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mia entrena para una maratón desde marzo, pero no se cree corredora.»

feedback.es: Train for a marathon es la colocación natural; preparing for también es posible, pero no suena tan fijo para un deporte.

origin.text: Mia has been ___ for a marathon since March, yet she still describes herself as “not a real runner”. Her colleague finds that rather charming.

es: Usar encabezamientos (That film, it was brilliant) y colas (She's lovely, your sister) con el pronombre obligatorio y concordante, como en la gramática oral, para evaluar personas y cosas.

teaching.en: That new series on Friday, it was absolutely brilliant, and I would happily watch the whole thing again.
teaching.es: Esa serie nueva del viernes, fue absolutamente genial, y volvería a verla entera con gusto.
teaching.explanationEs: Cabeza: el tema va primero y el pronombre it lo retoma antes del comentario.
segments: That new series on Friday, it was absolutely brilliant,
and I would happily watch the whole thing again.
teaching.audioText: That new series on Friday, it was absolutely brilliant, and I would happily watch the whole thing again.

teaching.en: Your grandmother, she's lovely, and she's a real character too, always telling stories that nobody quite believes.
teaching.es: Tu abuela, qué encanto, y además es todo un personaje, siempre contando historias que nadie se cree del todo.
teaching.explanationEs: El pronombre concuerda con el tema: grandmother → she. Puedes sumar un segundo comentario.
segments: Your grandmother, she's lovely, and she's a real character
too, always telling stories that nobody quite believes.
teaching.audioText: Your grandmother, she's lovely, and she's a real character too, always telling stories that nobody quite believes.

teaching.en: She's an amazing cook, that woman next door, and she never forgets to invite half of the street.
teaching.es: Es una cocinera increíble, esa mujer de al lado, y nunca se olvida de invitar a media calle.
teaching.explanationEs: Cola: la frase completa va primero y el tema se añade al final, a menudo para dejar claro de quién hablas.
segments: She's an amazing cook, that woman next door, and
she never forgets to invite half of the street.
teaching.audioText: She's an amazing cook, that woman next door, and she never forgets to invite half of the street.

teaching.en: They're never quiet, my next-door neighbours, but I can't say I mind, because the parties are good fun.
teaching.es: Nunca están callados, mis vecinos de al lado, pero no me molesta, porque las fiestas son muy divertidas.
teaching.explanationEs: Con un tema plural, la cola usa they: neighbours → they're.
segments: They're never quiet, my next-door neighbours, but I can't
say I mind, because the parties are good fun.
teaching.audioText: They're never quiet, my next-door neighbours, but I can't say I mind, because the parties are good fun.

teaching.en: It's terribly noisy, that café, isn't it? I can never get on with places where everybody has to shout.
teaching.es: Es terriblemente ruidoso, ese café, ¿verdad? Nunca me llevo bien con los sitios donde todos tienen que gritar.
teaching.explanationEs: Con cola, la tag va al final y repite el auxiliar de la frase: It's → isn't it.
segments: It's terribly noisy, that café, isn't it? I can never
get on with places where everybody has to shout.
teaching.audioText: It's terribly noisy, that café, isn't it? I can never get on with places where everybody has to shout.

teaching.en: I have a soft spot for him, our line manager: he would bend over backwards for anyone, such a lovely man.
teaching.es: Le tengo debilidad, a nuestro jefe directo: haría lo imposible por cualquiera, es un hombre encantador.
teaching.explanationEs: Si el tema es el objeto, la cola usa him, her, it o them: I have a soft spot for him.
segments: I have a soft spot for him, our line manager: he
would bend over backwards for anyone, such a lovely man.
teaching.audioText: I have a soft spot for him, our line manager: he would bend over backwards for anyone, such a lovely man.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mis vecinos de al lado, nunca están callados después de las diez.»

answer.text: My next-door neighbours, they're never quiet after ten
accepted: My next-door neighbours, they're never quiet after ten
They're never quiet after ten, my next-door neighbours

feedback.es: El tema plural (neighbours) se retoma con they; la cabeza abre la frase y la cola la cierra, y las dos órdenes son válidas.

hint.es: El pronombre del tema plural es they; puedes poner el tema primero o al final.

prompt.es: Completa: «Tu hermana, qué persona tan encantadora es.»

feedback.es: Tras la cabeza (Your sister) hace falta un pronombre que concuerde: she. Sin él, la frase suena a calco del español.

hint.es: Un pronombre femenino singular + el verbo be.

origin.text: Your sister, ___ such a lovely person. She always remembers everyone's birthday.

prompt.es: ¿Qué cola usa bien el pronombre y la tag para quejarse del vecino?

choices.text: He's far too noisy, that neighbour of mine, isn't it?
It's far too noisy, that neighbour of mine, isn't he?
He's far too noisy, that neighbour of mine, isn't he?

feedback.es: El tema es una persona (he) y la tag repite el mismo pronombre: isn't he. Mezclar he con it rompe la concordancia.

hint.es: El pronombre y la tag deben concordar con el tema.

origin.text: Tom's new neighbour keeps the whole street awake at night, and Tom is complaining about him to a friend.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo nombra Ana a la persona de la que habla en su última frase?

choices.text: By naming him at the start, before the comment.
By repeating Leo's auxiliary with a pronoun.
By asking Leo to agree with a question tag.
By naming him at the end, after the comment.

feedback.es: Ana empieza con el comentario (Mine's useless) y añade my line manager al final: es una cola. Is she? es un eco, pero habla de otra cosa.

origin.text: Leo: “The new manager, she's absolutely brilliant. She'd bend over backwards for the team.” Ana: “Is she? Mine's useless, my line manager, and he never answers an email.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra el hablante hacia sus vecinos.

choices.text: Warm towards them, even though they can be annoying at times.
Annoyed by everyone except the quiet mother.
Pleased with the father but tired of the children.
Bored by them, because the speaker hardly ever sees them.

feedback.es: Hay quejas (ruido, historias) pero el hablante cierra con «a soft spot for the whole family» y no quiere que se vayan: afecto pese a las molestias.

origin.audio: I'll tell you about the people next door. The father, he's a real character, always telling stories nobody believes. The mother, she's very quiet, the sort you hardly notice. Lovely woman, though. And the children? Noisy. Terribly noisy, those two. Still, I have a soft spot for the whole family, and I wouldn't want them to move.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Haría lo imposible por cualquiera, ese jefe nuestro.»

answer.text: He would bend over backwards for anybody, that line manager of ours
accepted: He would bend over backwards for anybody, that line manager of ours
That line manager of ours, he would bend over backwards for anybody

feedback.es: La cola nombra al jefe al final y he concuerda con él; bend over backwards se mantiene junto como expresión fija.

prompt.es: Reescribe la frase con cabeza, como en una charla informal.

answer.text: My line manager, she's absolutely brilliant, and she never shouts at the team.
accepted: My line manager, she's absolutely brilliant, and she never shouts at the team.
My line manager, she is absolutely brilliant, and she never shouts at the team.
My line manager, he's absolutely brilliant, and he never shouts at the team.

feedback.es: La cabeza saca el tema (my line manager) y un pronombre concordante (she o he, según la persona) lo retoma antes del comentario.

origin.text: Frase escrita: «My line manager is absolutely brilliant, and she never shouts at the team.» Reescríbela poniendo el tema primero y un pronombre que lo retome.

evidenceGroups: never shouts at the whole team

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué actitud muestra Sara hacia su jefe.

choices.text: Proud of him because he treats every client the same.
Supportive of him in spite of his faults.
Tired of him, although she admits he is good with clients.
Embarrassed by him, so she rarely mentions him to Mia.

feedback.es: Sara enumera defectos pero termina con «a soft spot» y «I wouldn't swap him»: cariño pese a los fallos, no cansancio ni vergüenza.

origin.audio: Sara was telling Mia about her new line manager. “Honestly, he's a real character, that man. Absolutely brilliant with clients, but he hardly ever answers an email. And his moods! Quiet for weeks, and then he shouts at everybody over nothing, even over a missing pen. Still, I have a soft spot for him. Last month he worked all weekend so that we could finish the project, and he never once complained. He'd bend over backwards for any of us, you know.” Mia smiled. “He sounds hard work, your line manager.” “Oh, he is,” said Sara. “But I wouldn't swap him for anyone.”

prompt.es: Completa: «No me llevo bien con ellos, esos vecinos de arriba.»

feedback.es: Get on with alguien significa llevarse bien con esa persona; la cola those neighbours of mine concreta de quién hablas.

origin.text: “How are you finding the people upstairs?” “Honestly, I can't ___ on with them, those neighbours of mine. They play loud music at midnight.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender el hablante sobre el hermano de su amigo?

choices.text: That he is dishonest and cannot be trusted at all.
That he is as careful with money as the speaker's brother.
That he is generous but careless about money.
That he is rich enough not to worry about money.

feedback.es: «A real character» y las rondas para desconocidos sugieren generosidad despreocupada; el texto no dice que sea deshonesto ni que gane más.

origin.text: “My brother, he's brilliant with money. Saves every cent, that one. Your brother, though, he's a different story, isn't he? A real character, always buying drinks for strangers and promising to pay everybody back next month.”

prompt.es: Reescribe la frase con cola, como en una charla informal.

answer.text: She's an amazing cook, the woman next door.
accepted: She's an amazing cook, the woman next door.
She is an amazing cook, the woman next door.
She's an absolutely brilliant cook, the woman next door.

feedback.es: La cola pone primero la frase con pronombre (she) y añade el tema al final para aclarar de quién hablas.

origin.text: Frase escrita: «The woman next door is an amazing cook.» Reescríbela con la frase primero y el tema al final.

prompt.es: ¿Con qué propósito usa Mia tantas colas en este mensaje?

choices.text: To correct a mistake that her friend had made earlier.
To keep her message short enough for a busy reader.
To avoid repeating the name of the person she mentions.
To give warm, friendly opinions about people and things.

feedback.es: Las colas añaden valoraciones cálidas y cercanas (lovely, brilliant, a soft spot); no corrigen ni acortan el mensaje.

origin.text: Mia wrote: “Lovely evening, honestly. The food, it was absolutely brilliant, and the host was a real character, your cousin. Quiet at first, that man, then he never stopped talking! I do have a soft spot for him now. He went out of his way to find me a taxi, and it was raining.”

prompt.es: Ordena: «Son absolutamente geniales, tus vecinos.»

feedback.es: Tema plural, pronombre they: la cola nombra a los vecinos al final, aunque también funciona con la cabeza delante.

es: Recuperar lo que se omite o se sustituye en réplicas rápidas (I'd love to, So have I, Neither did she, I hope so, I'm afraid not) y deducir qué piensa quien responde.

teaching.en: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to, but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”
teaching.es: Para rechazar una invitación con cortesía, empieza con calidez: «Me encantaría, pero me temo que estoy desbordado de trabajo hasta el viernes.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd love to omite el verbo que ya se dijo (come): solo queda to. Después del but llega la razón.
segments: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to,
but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”
teaching.audioText: To decline an invitation politely, start warmly: “I'd love to, but I'm afraid I'm swamped with work until Friday.”

teaching.en: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”
teaching.es: «Estoy absolutamente agotado después de ese viaje.» «Yo también. Casi no podía mantener los ojos abiertos en el tren.»
teaching.explanationEs: So + auxiliar + sujeto = yo también. El auxiliar es el de la frase original: am.
segments: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I
could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”
teaching.audioText: “I'm absolutely exhausted after that journey.” “So am I. I could hardly keep my eyes open on the train.”

teaching.en: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”
teaching.es: «Anoche no dormí muy bien.» «Yo tampoco. Los vecinos estuvieron gritando hasta casi las tres.»
teaching.explanationEs: Neither + auxiliar + sujeto = yo tampoco; el auxiliar copia didn't y el verbo se omite.
segments: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did
I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”
teaching.audioText: “I didn't sleep very well last night.” “Neither did I. The neighbours were shouting until almost three o'clock.”

teaching.en: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”
teaching.es: «¿Estarán despejadas las carreteras cuando salgamos?» «Eso espero. El pronóstico dice que la nieve parará antes del mediodía.»
teaching.explanationEs: So sustituye a toda la oración (the roads will be clear). En negativo: I hope not.
segments: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I
hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”
teaching.audioText: “Will the roads be clear by the time we leave?” “I hope so. The forecast says the snow should stop by midday.”

teaching.en: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”
teaching.es: «¿Estará Tom ocupado toda la tarde?» «Me temo que sí, y más bien dudo que tenga tiempo para nosotros antes de las seis.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid so / not da una mala noticia con educación y sustituye a toda la oración.
segments: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and
I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”
teaching.audioText: “Will Tom be tied up all afternoon?” “I'm afraid so, and I rather doubt he'll have time for us before six.”

teaching.en: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”
teaching.es: «¿Nos lo saltamos esta noche?» «Preferiría que no. Estoy totalmente de acuerdo en que estamos rendidos, pero se ofenderían.»
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather not omite el verbo de la propuesta (give it a miss). I couldn't agree more refuerza un acuerdo.
segments: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I
couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”
teaching.audioText: “Shall we give it a miss tonight?” “I'd rather not. I couldn't agree more that we're worn out, but they'd be hurt.”

prompt.es: ¿Qué se omite tras «I'd love to» en la respuesta de Leo?

choices.text: help his cousin move
have a few friends over
phone her at six
stay for dinner afterwards

feedback.es: I'd love to deja solo to: el verbo omitido es el de la pregunta de Mia (stay for dinner afterwards). Lo demás son otros datos del texto.

answer.text:
Tom: So, are we booking the flights for the weekend in Seville tonight?
Mia: To be honest, I'd rather wait a day. The prices went up again this morning, and my landlord still hasn't returned my deposit.
Tom: Fair enough. By the way, did you speak to Sara about the hotel?
Mia: Not yet. She's been swamped all week, hasn't she?
Tom: She has. Anyway, let's get back to the flights. If we leave on Friday evening, it would be cheaper, wouldn't it?
Mia: Probably. Come to think of it, Carlos mentioned a cheap airline last month. Shall I ask him?
Tom: Good idea. Actually, I'll text him now. And for what it's worth, I'd happily pay a bit more for a morning flight.
Mia: Mind you, a morning flight means getting up at five. Honestly, I'd rather sleep.
Tom: Fair enough. Let's decide tomorrow, then.

Mia: Are we meeting at your flat on Saturday to plan the trip?
Tom: Honestly, I'd rather go out. My kitchen is a mess, and I have no time to clean it, to be frank.
Mia: No problem. Let's book a table somewhere, shall we?
Tom: Sure. By the way, did you know Sara has a new flat? It's lovely, apparently.

feedback.es: Un buen intercambio vuelve al plan con anyway, cambia de tema con by the way, opina con to be honest, recuerda con come to think of it y cierra alguna frase con una tag.

origin.audio: Every family dinner in our house follows the same pattern. Somebody begins with a serious subject, like the landlord or the price of flights, and within two minutes my aunt has drifted off into a story about her neighbour's dog. “Anyway,” my father says, always in the same tired voice, “where were we?” By then, of course, nobody remembers. Come to think of it, that may be the point. To be honest, I suspect we all enjoy the detours more than the decisions, and my father, mind you, is usually the one who starts them.

prompt.es: Escribe una sobremesa de unas 170 palabras con los cuatro recursos.

answer.text:
Tom: By the way, have you heard the gossip about Mia? She's moving to Madrid.
Sara: No way! Is she? Since when?
Tom: Since last week. Her company, it offered her a great job there.
Carlos: Did it? Good for her. To be honest, she always wanted to live abroad.
Sara: She's very brave, Mia, isn't she?
Tom: Very. I'd miss her, though. She's a lovely friend.
Carlos: So would I. Anyway, this soup, it's delicious. Did you make it, Sara?
Sara: I did. My grandmother, she gave me the recipe.
Carlos: Did she? Lucky you. Mind you, I couldn't eat another bite, and I'd love to try the dessert.
Sara: Go on, then. Help yourself. Shall we do the dishes afterwards?
Carlos: I'd love that. Thank you both.
Sara: And Tom still has to propose a toast.
Tom: So I do! Cheers, everyone. To Mia, and to her new job!

feedback.es: Una buena sobremesa propone un tema con marcador, reacciona con ecos o elipsis, usa cabeza o cola y cambia de tema con otro marcador.

origin.text: Situación: sobremesa en casa de Sara con Carlos y Tom. Tom propone un tema con una noticia (Mia se muda a Madrid). Escribe el intercambio (Sara/Carlos/Tom) de unas 170 palabras con: el tema propuesto con un marcador, dos reacciones (un eco y una elipsis), una cabeza o una cola y un cambio de tema con un marcador.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué pregunta Sara por el postre.

choices.text: To hint that the meal should finish soon.
To check that Carlos had not eaten everything.
To tease Tom about his strong opinions.
To move the talk away from a subject causing tension.

feedback.es: Sara lo pregunta con naturalidad justo después de la discusión por el dinero, y Tom «realised what she was doing»: es una maniobra para alejar la charla de la tensión, no una pregunta sobre el postre.

origin.audio: The dinner had been going well until Tom began to argue about money again. Mia had stopped eating, and nobody was looking at anyone else. Sara, who was the host, caught Mia's eye. “Has anyone tried the dessert yet?” she asked brightly. “I have,” said Carlos, “and I'll polish off whatever is left.” Everybody laughed, including Tom, who realised what she was doing. “Fair enough,” he said. “I'll stop. Mind you, I was right.” That has become a running joke at their table: Tom is always right, and always told to stop.

feedback.es: La cola nombra a tu hermano al final y la tag isn't he? concuerda con he; también funciona con la cabeza delante.

prompt.es: ¿Qué sugiere el texto sobre la reacción de los invitados?

choices.text: That their reaction was cooler than Carlos had hoped.
That they doubted that his sister had really been offered it.
That they were upset by his sister's good luck.
That Carlos had not explained the news clearly.

feedback.es: Un eco sin pregunta de seguimiento y el silencio posterior indican interés escaso; Sara lo nota y cambia de tema por cortesía. El texto no habla de envidia ni de dudas.

origin.text: After the meal, Carlos told the table that his sister had been offered a job abroad. “Has she?” said Mia. “That's something.” Nobody asked where, or what the job was. Sara looked at Carlos, who was staring at his plate, and quickly offered more coffee. Mia asked for more bread, and the talk moved on to the weather.

prompt.es: Escucha y deduce qué piensa realmente el hablante de la comida.

choices.text: It was good enough that the speaker ate three plates willingly.
It was poor, but the speaker kept quiet out of kindness.
It was poor, and the speaker said so openly to his brother.
It was ordinary, and the speaker was simply very hungry.

feedback.es: El hablante dice que su hermano cocina fatal y confiesa que comió tres platos por educación y sin decir palabra: no le gustó y lo disimuló.

origin.audio: “My brother, he's a terrible cook. Burns everything, that man.” “Is he? I thought he made the pasta.” “He did, and I ate three plates of it out of kindness. Honestly, I don't know how I finished them, and I certainly didn't say a word.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Cada Navidad cuenta la misma historia y ya es una broma recurrente.»

feedback.es: A running joke es la colocación para una broma que se repite con el tiempo; running gag también existe, pero es más propia del teatro y la televisión.

origin.text: Every Christmas my uncle tells the same story about the burnt chicken, and it has become a running ___ in our family.
